memories.body: Use pnpm for JavaScript projects; never commit package-lock.json.
Commit messages are short, imperative and in English, without a scope prefix.
When fixing a bug, add a failing test first, then the fix.
Customer-facing UI copy is in Bosnian unless the project says otherwise; code and comments are in English.
New TypeScript code uses strict mode and no `any`; prefer `unknown` with a type guard.
Prettier with 2-space indent, double quotes, trailing commas and print width 120.
Store timestamps in UTC and convert to Europe/Sarajevo only when displaying them.
Keep money as integer minor units (cents, feninga) and format at the edge; floats drift in VAT math.
Secrets live in .env files that are never committed; add each new variable to .env.example with a placeholder.
Keep changes small: one concern per pull request, under about 300 changed lines.
Touch targets are at least 44×44 points on iOS and 48×48 dp on Android.
Serve product images as WebP or AVIF with explicit width and height so the layout doesn't shift while they load.
Retry only idempotent requests, with exponential backoff and jitter, at most 3 times; never retry a payment capture blindly.
Ask before adding a new runtime dependency; prefer the platform or what the project already uses.
Global state lives in Zustand stores under src/stores; server data goes through React Query and never into Zustand.
Navigation uses Expo Router with file-based routes in app/; the tabs are Shop, Try-on, Cart and Account.
All HTTP calls go through src/api/client.ts, a fetch wrapper that adds the auth token and base URL; screens never call fetch directly.
Styles use StyleSheet.create at the bottom of each file; colors and spacing come from src/theme/tokens.ts.
Product grids use FlashList with estimatedItemSize; FlatList stuttered with 500+ frame thumbnails.
Product photos load through expo-image with a disk cache policy; the CDN serves them resized to 3x.
The cart is persisted with the zustand persist middleware to AsyncStorage under the key cart-v2.
Public config uses EXPO_PUBLIC_ variables read in app.config.ts; nothing secret ships inside the app.
Builds go through EAS: the preview profile (internal distribution) for testers, the production profile for the stores; OTA updates go to the production channel only after QA.
Component tests use React Native Testing Library with jest-expo; query by role or label, and use testID only when nothing else works.
Try-on uses react-native-vision-camera with a frame processor for face landmarks; Expo Camera was too slow.
Push notifications don't arrive on some Xiaomi devices when the app is killed; battery optimization is the suspect.
Strings live in src/i18n/bs.json and en.json through i18next; keys are screen.element, for example cart.checkoutButton.
Card payments go through the web checkout in an in-app browser (expo-web-browser); there is no native payment SDK.
Customizations live in a child theme of Storefront (optics-child); the parent theme is never edited.
Business logic goes in the site plugin wp-content/plugins/optics-core, not in functions.php.
All hooks, functions and options are prefixed optics_ to avoid clashes with other plugins.
Lens options (index, coating, tint) are WooCommerce product add-ons, priced per option and stored as order item meta.
Customers upload prescriptions as PDF or JPG on the product page; files go to a non-public folder and are served through a signed download link.
Pages are cached with LiteSpeed Cache; cart, checkout and my-account are excluded.
Deploys go over SFTP from GitHub Actions to cPanel; the database is never pushed, only pulled down to staging.
Changes are tried on the staging site first; after pulling the database, run a WP-CLI search-replace for the URL.
Sanitize every input with sanitize_text_field or absint, escape output with esc_html or esc_attr, and put a nonce on every form.
Order emails went to spam until mail was sent through the provider's SMTP with SPF and DKIM set up (WP Mail SMTP).
Prices are entered including 17% VAT and shown including tax in the shop and the cart.
Shipping is free over 100 KM, otherwise a flat 7 KM by courier; pickup in the store is free.
Product titles follow 'Brand Model – Frame colour'; meta descriptions are written by hand for the top 50 products.
Controllers stay thin: validation in Form Requests, logic in service classes under app/Services, repositories only for complex queries.
The API uses Laravel Sanctum personal access tokens; the web dashboard uses session cookies.
Long work (PDF parsing, model calls) runs on Redis queues with Horizon, never inside a request.
Tax answers are generated by the model from retrieved law excerpts, and every answer cites the article it used.
Feature tests use Pest with RefreshDatabase on in-memory SQLite; outside HTTP calls are faked with Http::fake().
Amounts are stored as integer feninga in BIGINT columns and cast to a Money value object.
Migrations are never edited after merge; add a new one. Columns are snake_case and foreign keys constrained.
API errors are JSON problem details (type, title, status, detail); validation errors keep Laravel's 422 shape.
Tax rates and thresholds live in the tax_rules table keyed by year, not in config files.
Official law texts come from the Official Gazette PDFs; scanned ones need OCR before chunking.
Deploys go through Laravel Forge to one VPS with zero-downtime releases; maintenance mode only for migrations that lock tables.
Parsing large PDFs with smalot/pdfparser ran out of memory; process them page by page in a queued job.
Dates in API responses are ISO 8601 in UTC; number formatting is left to the client.
App Router only: server components by default, 'use client' only for the 3D viewer and interactive forms.
The try-on viewer uses three.js through @react-three/fiber; glasses models are Draco-compressed glTF files under 1 MB each.
Face tracking runs in the browser with MediaPipe Face Landmarker (WASM); no camera video leaves the device.
Tailwind only, no CSS modules; design tokens in tailwind.config.ts and component variants with cva.
Data is fetched in server components with fetch and revalidation tags; client components receive it as props.
The SaaS dashboard signs in with Auth.js email magic links; organizations own the API keys for the embed widget.
Shops embed try-on with a script tag that mounts an iframe; the iframe and the host page talk through postMessage with origin checks.
Hosted on Vercel: a preview deployment per pull request, production from main.
Load the MediaPipe WASM and model lazily when the user opens try-on, not on page load; LCP dropped from 4.1 s to 1.9 s.
Playwright covers the embed flow end to end; Vitest covers utilities.
Server-only secrets never get the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix; env is validated at startup with a zod schema in src/env.ts.
Billing uses Stripe subscriptions (Starter, Growth, Enterprise) with usage counted per try-on session.
The dashboard is English only; Bosnian and German translations are planned but not started.
PostgreSQL 16 through node-postgres; SQL is written by hand in src/db/queries, no ORM.
Schema changes are node-pg-migrate migrations in migrations/, one per change, never edited after deploy.
Every request body is validated with a zod schema in the route file; invalid input returns 400 with the zod issues.
Errors bubble to one Express error handler that logs with pino and answers {error: {code, message}}.
Orders from the WooCommerce shop arrive by webhook; the handler verifies the signature and enqueues, a worker writes to Postgres.
WooCommerce retries webhooks: store the delivery id and ignore repeats, or orders get created twice.
Background jobs use pg-boss on the same Postgres instead of Redis.
Integration tests run against a throwaway Postgres (testcontainers); unit tests mock nothing but the clock.
Log JSON with pino and never log request bodies of payment or customer endpoints.
Runs in Docker on the shop's VPS; GitHub Actions deploys with docker compose pull and up -d.
The service is ESM only (type: module) and imports include the .js extension.
Internal calls are signed with a shared HMAC header; this service has no user accounts.

episodes.problem: The try-on screen crashed after adding react-native-svg.
episodes.error:
Invariant Violation: requireNativeComponent: "RNSVGPath" was not found in the UIManager.

This error is located at:
    in RNSVGPath
    in FrameOutline (at src/screens/TryOn.tsx:42)
episodes.fix: Rebuilt the development client after installing react-native-svg (expo prebuild and a new EAS development build); the installed client didn't have the native module.
episodes.lesson: A 'was not found in the UIManager' error right after adding a native package means the installed app predates it: rebuild the native app or development client.

episodes.problem: Metro couldn't resolve imports that use the @ alias.
episodes.error:
error: Error: Unable to resolve module @/theme/tokens from /Users/f/eyewear-app/src/components/PriceTag.tsx: @/theme/tokens could not be found within the project or in these directories:
  node_modules
episodes.fix: Added the @ alias to babel.config.js (babel-plugin-module-resolver) to match the tsconfig paths, then cleared the Metro cache with expo start -c.
episodes.lesson: Path aliases have to be configured for Metro (babel module-resolver) as well as TypeScript; clear the Metro cache after changing them.

episodes.problem: pod install failed after adding VisionCamera.
episodes.error:
[!] CocoaPods could not find compatible versions for pod "VisionCamera":
  In Podfile:
    VisionCamera (from `../node_modules/react-native-vision-camera`)

Specs satisfying the `VisionCamera` dependency were found, but they required a higher minimum deployment target.
episodes.fix: Raised the iOS deployment target to 15.1 with expo-build-properties in app.config.ts and ran pod install again.
episodes.lesson: When CocoaPods says a pod requires a higher minimum deployment target, raise the iOS deployment target (expo-build-properties in Expo) instead of pinning an older pod.

episodes.problem: The product grid crashed while products were loading.
episodes.error:
TypeError: Cannot read property 'map' of undefined
    at ProductGrid (src/components/ProductGrid.tsx:18:25)
episodes.fix: Defaulted products to an empty array while the React Query request is loading (data ?? []).
episodes.lesson: Default query data to an empty array before mapping it; React Query returns undefined until the first fetch completes.

episodes.problem: The cart crashed with a fatal error for a deleted product.
episodes.error: PHP Fatal error:  Uncaught Error: Call to a member function get_price() on bool in /home/optics/public_html/wp-content/plugins/optics-core/includes/lens-pricing.php:57
episodes.fix: wc_get_product() returns false for deleted products; return early when the product is missing before reading its price.
episodes.lesson: wc_get_product() returns false for missing or deleted products: check the result before calling methods on it.

episodes.problem: The product export ran out of memory.
episodes.error: PHP Fatal error:  Allowed memory size of 268435456 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 20480 bytes) in /home/optics/public_html/wp-includes/class-wpdb.php on line 2187
episodes.fix: The export loaded every order at once; switched to wc_get_orders with paged batches of 200.
episodes.lesson: When a WordPress export or loop exhausts the allowed memory size, page through records in batches instead of raising memory_limit.

episodes.problem: The prescription upload form failed with an expired link message on cached pages.
episodes.error: The link you followed has expired. Please try again.
episodes.fix: LiteSpeed cached the product page with a stale nonce; the form now fetches a fresh nonce with AJAX before submitting.
episodes.lesson: 'The link you followed has expired' on a cached page is a stale nonce: fetch the nonce with AJAX or keep the form out of the page cache.

episodes.problem: A query still used a renamed column.
episodes.error: SQLSTATE[42S22]: Column not found: 1054 Unknown column 'tax_year' in 'where clause' (Connection: mysql, SQL: select * from `tax_rules` where `tax_year` = 2026)
episodes.fix: The column became year in a new migration but TaxRule::scopeForYear still used tax_year; updated the scope.
episodes.lesson: After renaming a column, search query scopes and raw where clauses for the old name; SQLite tests only catch it if they hit that query.

episodes.problem: Token tests failed in a fresh Laravel 11 app.
episodes.error: Illuminate\Database\QueryException: SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 1 no such table: personal_access_tokens (Connection: sqlite, SQL: insert into "personal_access_tokens" ("name", "token") values (api, 8f2c))
episodes.fix: Sanctum's migration wasn't published; ran php artisan install:api, which installs Sanctum and publishes it.
episodes.lesson: In Laravel 11, 'no such table: personal_access_tokens' means Sanctum isn't installed yet: run php artisan install:api.

episodes.problem: The law PDF parsing job kept failing after retries.
episodes.error: Illuminate\Queue\MaxAttemptsExceededException: App\Jobs\ParseLawPdf has been attempted too many times.
episodes.fix: The job ran longer than retry_after (90 s), so a worker picked it up again; set timeout 600 and retry_after 660 on the pdf queue.
episodes.lesson: MaxAttemptsExceededException on a long job usually means retry_after is shorter than the job's runtime; keep the job timeout below retry_after.

episodes.problem: The price badge caused a hydration error.
episodes.error:
Error: Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client. As a result this tree will be regenerated on the client.
  at PriceBadge (src/components/PriceBadge.tsx:12:9)
episodes.fix: The badge used toLocaleString(), which differs between Node and the browser; the price is now formatted on the server with Intl.NumberFormat('bs-BA') and passed down as a string.
episodes.lesson: Hydration mismatches often come from number or date formatting that differs between server and browser: format on the server or use a fixed locale.

episodes.error:
ReferenceError: window is not defined
    at Viewer (src/components/TryOnViewer.tsx:8:3)
episodes.fix: Loaded the viewer with next/dynamic and ssr: false.
episodes.lesson: 'window is not defined' in Next.js means browser-only code ran on the server: load that component with next/dynamic and ssr: false, or touch window inside useEffect.

episodes.problem: The embedded widget couldn't read the host page.
episodes.error: SecurityError: Failed to read a named property 'document' from 'Window': Blocked a frame with origin "https://tryon.example" from accessing a cross-origin frame.
episodes.fix: Replaced direct access to the parent window with postMessage and an origin check on both sides.
episodes.lesson: Cross-origin iframes can't touch each other's DOM: talk through postMessage and check event.origin on both sides.

episodes.problem: The worker container couldn't reach Postgres.
episodes.error:
Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432
    at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect [as oncomplete] (node:net:1611:16)
episodes.fix: Inside Docker the database host is the compose service name (db), not localhost; DATABASE_URL was updated for the container.
episodes.lesson: ECONNREFUSED to localhost from inside a container: localhost is the container itself, so use the compose service name or host.docker.internal.

episodes.problem: A seed script failed to import an ESM-only package.
episodes.error: Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: require() of ES Module /app/node_modules/node-fetch/src/index.js from /app/scripts/seed.cjs not supported.
episodes.fix: Converted the seed script to ESM (.mjs with import) instead of pinning node-fetch 2.
episodes.lesson: ERR_REQUIRE_ESM means the package is ESM-only: switch the caller to import (or a dynamic import()) instead of downgrading the package.

episodes.problem: Every WooCommerce webhook was rejected as invalid.
episodes.error:
Error: webhook signature mismatch
    at verifyWoo (src/webhooks/woo.ts:31:11)
episodes.fix: WooCommerce signs the raw body but express.json() had already parsed it; the webhook route now uses express.raw() and the HMAC is computed over the buffer.
episodes.lesson: Verify webhook HMAC signatures over the raw request body; a JSON body parser changes the bytes.
